rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND SECTION 32, ARTICLE VIII OF R.A. 7875, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'NATIONAL HEALTH INSURANCE ACT OF 1995'
rows.abstract: Rationale: "Art. 3 Sec. 32 of RA 7875, National Health Insurance Program, provides that accreditation shall be granted only to health care providers in operation for at least three (3) years. The 3-year period is too long for a good clinic or hospital to wait for accreditation ..." Amends, therefore, this Section to read as follows: "Sec. 32. Accreditation Eligibility-All Health care providers, as enumerated in Section 4 (0) hereof and operating for at elast one (1) year may apply for accreditation."

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTIONS 14, 15, AND 16 OF CHAPTER 5, TITLE III OF EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 292, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ADMINISTRATIVE CODE OF 1987 BY RENAMING THE PUBLIC ATTORNEY'S OFFICE AS THE 'PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE'
rows.abstract: Rationale: To be truly reflective of the lofty purpose of said office this bill seeks to change the name of the Public Attorney's Office to the PUBLIC DEFENDER'S OFFICE. A defender, after all, is a protector, advocate, champion, vindicator and upholder.  By renaming this office as the Public Defender, it will hopefully eradicate misperception that only the rich get justice and only the poor are aggrieved. It would give life to the often quoted message of the late President Ramon Magsaysay that"those who have less in life should have more in law."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1996-10-01

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE SAFE DRINKING WATER COMMISSION, SETTING STANDARDS FOR CLEAN AND SAFE PUBLIC DRINKING WATER SYSTEMS, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Clean, safe and abundant drinking water is one of our greatest patrimonial treasures, whether it comes from the ground or from lakes, streams or rivers.  We can't take if for grantedd. We must protect its purity andd integrity now - and for future generations. "Safe Drinking Water Act of 1996" Prescribes the composition of the Commission, its power and duties; states the PROHIBITED ACTS under this proposed measure andd prescribes penalties for violation thereof.

rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING ALL OFFICIAL NONWORKING DAYS TO FALL EITHER ON A MONDAY OR A FRIDAY
rows.abstract: Rationale: This measure proposes that all official non-working days should be mandatorily scheduled such that they either fall on a MOnday or a Friday.  This will adddress the problem of "intentional absenteeism" of workers and will therefore positively impact on productivity. The longer breaks are also expected to promote the health of the workers by giving them ample time for rest and attention to their personal needs outside off their works. Defines "official non-working days" as  ? in thisAct; prescribes the GUIDELINES to be followed in implementing this measure.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1996-10-02

rows.abstract: Proposes the following amendments to RA 6686 - "SEC. 1. rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING A LEVY OF TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT ON THE GROSS INCOME DERIVED FROM THE MANUFACTURE OF CONTAINERS, BAGS, BOTTLES, WRAPPERS, OR PACKAGES OF CONSUMER PRODUCTS WITH THE USE OF NON-BIODEGRADAB LE PLASTIC MATERIALS, AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FORVIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: Rationale: Plastic materials are very toxic when burned, emitting poisonous gases such as chlorine, sulfuric acid and cyanides which pollute the atmosphere. The effects of inhaling smoke from these materials can lead to inflammation of the mucous membrance in the respiratory tract, leadding to edema of the bronchial tubes and blood vessels in the lungs. Proposes the following schedule of paying the proposed levy: (1) 5% for the first year of implementation; (2) 10% for the second year; (3) 15%for the third year; (4) 20% for the fourth year; and (5) 25% for the fifth year and thereafter. Penalizes violation of this Act.

Society, therefore, should have the prerogative to recognize outstanding police andd military service. rows.abstract: Defines the nature of the proposed SPECIAL LOCAL DEVELOPMENT FUND  as follows --- "SEC. 1. Special Local Development Fund. - Ten percent (10%) of the national budget shall be allocated ffor the creation of a Special Local Development Fund (SLDF) which shall be used to improve the capacity of local government s to provide basic services. Fifty percent of the fund shall be channeled through the Land Bank of the Philippines (LBP) for lending to first class, second class and third class provinces,municipalitiess and barangays. The remaining fifty percent shall be used as grants to fourth class, fifth class andd sixth class provinces, municipalities andd barangays."

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO ALL BARANGAY OFFICIALS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 393 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: Rationale: The present laws, Republic Act No. 7160 and Republic Act No. 6942 while providing benefits to elected local officials overlooked an equally important aspect in government service which is retirement. With this bill the much needed assistance to our outgoing barangay officials will ultimately be met. Provides, therefore, for the following --- "SECTION 393. Benefits of Barangay Officials - xxx > (b) The punong barangay, the sangguniang barangay members, the barangay treasurer, and thebarangay secretary shall also: > (6) BE ENTITLED TO RETIREMENT BENEFITS FROM THE GSIS AFTER HAVING SERVED FOR AT LEAST NINE (9) YEARS OF CUMULATIVE SERVICE > PROVIDED, HOWEVER THAT A CERTAIN PERCENTAGE OF THE TOTAL OF THEIR MINIMUM BASIC ALLOWANCE ANNNUALLY SHALL BE REMITTED TO THE GSIS IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PROGRAM WHICH THE GSIS WILL ESTABLISH FOR THE PURPOSE; > PROVIDED, FURTHER THAT AT THE END OF NINE YEARS THE GSIS SHALL PAY THEM A LUMP SUM BENEFIT EQUIVALENT TO FIVE THOUSAND (P5,000.00) F

rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1.
